newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-PAY-AS-YOU-PLAY DEAL TAKES NDLOVU TO BIRMINGHAM.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-PAY-AS-YOU-PLAY DEAL TAKES NDLOVU TO BIRMINGHAM.

text.p: Zimbabwe international Peter Ndlovu's transfer from Premier League Coventry City to nearby Birmingham City of the First Division was resurrected on Monday with a rare pay-as-you-play agreement.
The 1.6 million pounds ($2.7 million) deal fell through last week because the 24-year-old forward failed a medical on an old knee injury.
But Birmingham have renegotiated the terms of the transfer with both Coventry and the player who will make the short 20-mile trip from Highfield Road to St Andrews with a four-year contract.
Birmingham will now pay Coventry a downpayment of just 200,000 pounds ($337,000), with the balance spread over the next three years.
But as Birmingham manager Trevor Francis explained: "The remainder of the fee is dependent on the player actually playing for us, otherwise we do not have to make further payments.
"The medical evidence suggests there is some risk involved because of his knee injury, but for 200,000 pounds we consider it a risk well worth taking."
Francis confirmed that a "large percentage" of Ndlovu's wages had also been renegotiated on the pay-as-you-play basis.
"The thing that convinced me to sign him is that the player himself has shown me he has a genuine desire to come and play for us," said Francis.
"He was willing to scrap the original contract and take the risk involved because he wants to play for Birmingham City and I applaud that.
"Hopefully its a deal that will work out for both parties."
Ndlovu joined Coventry for only 10,000 pounds ($16,200) from Highlanders of Zimbabwe in August 1991 and made over 150 appearances for the Sky Blues.

He is a highly-talented skilful player, and with his amazing ball control at speed can create chances for himself and the other forwards almost at will. If he is fully fit he will be a powerful weapon as Birmingham bid to gain promotion to the premier league.
Francis said on Monday that striker Ole Martin Aarst of Norwegian club Tromso is spending a week on trial at St Andrews with a view to a 1.8 million pounds ($3 million) transfer.
